UNDERSTANDING LINEAR INEQUALITIES
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what understanding linear inequalities means in plain words.
• Give one Kenyan example linked to Linear Inequalities.
• Correct one common mistake about this page.

INTRODUCTION

Use this anchor: Apply inequality symbols to inequality statements in learning situations. Clue from real life: Illustrate simple inequalities. Check every example on this page against that anchor.

MAIN NOTES
----
• An algebraic expression uses numbers and letters (variables) joined by operations.
• Like terms have the same variable part — combine them; unlike terms stay separate.
• To solve an equation, undo operations carefully on both sides.
• Check by substituting your answer back into the original equation.
• Example: if x = 4, then 2x + 7 = 15.

• Like terms have the same variable part — combine them; unlike terms stay separate.
• To solve an equation, undo operations carefully on both sides.
• Check by substituting your answer back into the original equation.
• Example: if x = 6, then 2x + 4 = 16.

Solve for x: x + 8 = 16.

Working:
1. Formula / relationship: x = RHS − constant
2. Substitute values: x = 16 − 8
3. x = 8
4. Check: 8 + 8 = 16
Final Answer: x = 8
